title: Vibhishana's crossing
hook: Ravana's own brother tells him the truth in council, is driven out, and comes to Rama for refuge
carry: sharanagati: I've come to Rama for refuge

segments.voice: Yesterday: the bridge, built in five days under Nala, and your line, nama, Rama's name carries the stones.

Go back to Lanka, just after Hanuman left it burning. Ravana calls his council. A monkey has walked into his city, killed his soldiers and set his houses on fire, and an army is gathering across the sea. The ministers stand up one by one, and every one says the same thing. You've beaten the gods, king. Who is this Rama? We'll crush him. It's the sound of a room where everyone has learned what the boss likes to hear. Then one person stands up and says something else.
screen: `RAVANA'S COUNCIL.` → `EVERYONE SAYS THE SAME THING.` → `ONE VOICE SAYS SOMETHING ELSE.`

segments.voice: It's Vibhishana, Ravana's younger brother. Valmiki places this before the bridge is built; we told the bridge first, and now we step back. Vibhishana speaks carefully, like someone who loves the person he's about to anger. Give Sita back. Taking another man's wife was wrong, and it will destroy you, and all of us with you. Rama has done you no harm. Return her, and Lanka lives. Ravana won't hear it. In Valmiki his answer is cruel: better to live with an enemy, or a cobra, than with a kinsman who secretly works for your enemy. He calls his brother a disgrace to the family, and says anyone else who spoke like this would be dead already. So Vibhishana rises into the air with four companions and speaks from above the hall. You're my elder brother, and I owe you respect. I said this for your good. People who say pleasant things are easy to find. People who say hard, useful things, and people willing to hear them, are rare. Then he leaves. He crosses the sea, stops in the sky above Rama's camp, and calls down: I am Ravana's brother, Vibhishana. I've left everything behind. I've come to Rama for refuge. Hindus have a word for what he does: sharanagati, taking refuge, coming to God with nothing and asking to be held. Tradition remembers Vibhishana as a model of it. He doesn't bring an army or a bargain. He says who he is, says he's left everything, and asks. What Rama does with that, tomorrow.
screen: `GIVE SITA BACK.` · `A KINSMAN WORSE THAN A COBRA.` · `I SAID IT FOR YOUR GOOD.` · `I'VE COME FOR REFUGE.` · then, large: `SHARANAGATI: TAKING REFUGE.`

segments.voice: Many Hindus have a short prayer of refuge they come back to. One is Sri Rama sharanam mama: Rama, you are my refuge. Sit quietly and bring to mind whatever you're carrying. If you pray, say it softly a few times, the way Vibhishana called down from the sky. If you don't pray, think of where you go when you need shelter, and let yourself arrive there for a few breaths.
Vibhishana's crossing. Ravana's younger brother speaks the truth in council, is called a traitor, and crosses the sea to ask Rama for refuge.
Your line: sharanagati, I've come to Rama for refuge. Tomorrow, Rama's camp decides what to do with him. Seven days, done.

howItsDone: Hindu tellers honor Vibhishana for his honest counsel in Ravana's hall, and Sri Vaishnava teachers hold up his coming to Rama as a model of sharanagati, taking refuge in God.

chat.meaning: Vibhishana told Ravana openly to give Sita back, for Ravana's own good. Driven out, he came to Rama with nothing and asked for refuge, which is why tradition honors him as a model of sharanagati.
